intent: The button that opens and closes its DropdownMenu's popup.
typical_uses: An icon-only "more" button beside a row or a card
A labelled button, such as an account name, that opens a menu of actions

dont_use_when.situation: A button that performs one action directly
An area that opens a menu on right-click

invariants.text: The trigger renders a native `<button>` with no kit styling of its own; a styled trigger comes from passing a Button through `render`.
The trigger carries `aria-haspopup="menu"`, so assistive technology announces it as a button that opens a menu.
Pressing the trigger toggles the menu; hovering opens it only when `openOnHover` is set, and `delay` and `closeDelay` take effect only then.

anti_patterns.dont: Leave an icon-only trigger without an accessible name
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `aria-label` to the trigger; it reaches the rendered button, and an icon alone gives the button no name

a11y.by: the primitive's Menu.Trigger renders a native <button> and sets aria-haspopup="menu"; dropdown-menu.test.tsx asserts the trigger is found by the button role and its accessible name 'Open'

children.states: children is the trigger's caption, or the caption of the element passed through render
children.because: `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more; the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

handle.states: handle is an opaque object from the primitive's Menu.createHandle(), tying this trigger to a DropdownMenu root it is not placed inside
handle.because: `MenuHandle<Payload>` is a class instance holding the menu's store, not data; the kit re-exports no createHandle, so a caller imports it from the primitive.

payload.states: payload is any value handed to the root's function children when this trigger opens the menu
payload.because: Typed by the caller's own `Payload` type parameter (`unknown` here), so no JSON Schema type can state what it holds.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the trigger's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the trigger's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, disabled). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; dropdown-menu.module.css styles no trigger, so the button keeps the look the caller gives it.

good.title: An outline Button as the trigger
An icon-only trigger with an accessible name

bad.title: A kit Button nested inside the trigger
bad.why: The trigger already renders a `<button>`, so this nests a button inside a button, which HTML does not allow; pass the Button through `render` instead.
